article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-dominant hybrid
Genetics: GMO × Donny Burger
Breeder: Skunk House Genetics
THC Content: 20-27%
CBD Content: Low to trace
Terpene Profile: myrcene , limonene , beta-caryophyllene
Primary Flavors: Garlic, diesel, black pepper, lemon, pine
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–9 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: late September to early October
Indoor Yield: Medium to high
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Moderate to advanced

Double Burger is what happens when a breeder decides that GMO genetics are not pungent enough already. Created by Skunk House Genetics from GMO × Donny Burger, this indica-dominant hybrid reinforces the garlic, fuel, Chem, and savory qualities of its family instead of diluting them with fruit or dessert genetics. Donny Burger is itself closely related to GMO, so the cross effectively concentrates a genetic line famous for oversized aroma, resin production , and a powerful body-heavy cannabis experience.

The flower can smell less like conventional sweet weed and more like a strange combination of black pepper, garlic, gasoline, lemon cleaner, damp earth, and caramelized onion. Potency follows the aroma. Commercial examples have reached more than 30% THCA, while the cultivar is generally regarded as strong enough that experienced consumers are its natural audience. One current Double Burger flower listing, for example, reports 35.015% THCA with myrcene, limonene, and caryophyllene as its three leading terpenes.
Genetics and Lineage

The official genetic formula associated with Double Burger is GMO × Donny Burger, with Skunk House Genetics responsible for the breeding work. Donny Burger, sometimes called GMO BX, comes from GMO crossed with Han Solo Burger . This means GMO appears repeatedly in the Double Burger family tree, deliberately reinforcing the traits that made the original cultivar distinctive. Prime Cuts Nursery likewise identifies Double Burger as GMO × Donny Burger and attributes the cross to Skunk House Genetics.

That repeated GMO influence explains much of the strain’s identity. GMO carries the celebrated Chem D × Forum Cookies background and became famous for its garlic, mushroom, onion, chemical, and fuel-like aroma. Han Solo Burger introduced additional OG and Kush influence into Donny Burger before the line was crossed back toward GMO again. Consequently, Double Burger is not simply another cultivar with “Burger” attached to its name. It represents a concentrated branch of modern Chem-derived marijuana breeding, where savory terpenes, heavy trichome development, dense flowers, and deep physical effects take priority over candy sweetness.

The importance of Double Burger can also be seen in what came after it. Skunk House Genetics used the cultivar extensively in later breeding projects, including Triple Burger, Double Solo Burger, and Hash Burger. Nasha Hash identifies Hash Burger as Han Solo Hash Plant × Double Burger, demonstrating how the plant became a building block for additional resin-oriented Burger genetics.
Effects and Experience

Double Burger generally wastes little time announcing its potency. The early portion can produce a strong head change accompanied by improved mood, mental quiet, and a brief period of heightened engagement. Some consumers find themselves talkative or focused during this stage, but the sensation is rarely as bright or restless as a traditional sativa. Instead, the cerebral component feels anchored by an increasingly obvious physical calm.

As the high matures, relaxation becomes the dominant feature. Limbs may feel heavier, muscular tension less noticeable, and the motivation to remain highly active can gradually fade. Moderate doses may still leave an experienced cannabis consumer comfortable enough to socialize, watch a movie, play games, or finish simple tasks. Larger servings are much more likely to turn the experience toward an evening on the couch, especially when the flower comes from a high-potency batch.

Its strength deserves particular attention. A commercial indoor example has tested at 35.015% THCA and nearly 40% total cannabinoids, illustrating just how powerful some expressions can become. High doses may cause dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, impaired short-term memory, anxiety, or excessive sedation. Anyone unfamiliar with strong marijuana should approach Double Burger conservatively rather than assuming its relaxed personality means it is mild.
Medical Benefits

For medical marijuana patients, the heavy physical side of Double Burger may be attractive when relaxation is more important than stimulation. Cannabis consumers sometimes choose similarly potent indica-leaning chemotypes when temporary discomfort, muscular tension, appetite loss, stress, or difficulty settling down interferes with the latter part of the day. Its tendency to progress from mental relief toward a stronger body sensation also helps explain why many people reserve Burger-family cultivars for afternoon or evening use.

The terpene composition provides additional context but should not be treated as a prescription. Tested Double Burger products have shown myrcene, limonene, and beta-caryophyllene among prominent compounds, while concentrated preparations have also contained linalool, humulene, bisabolol, and pinene. One laboratory analysis of Double Burger live rosin measured 7.93% total terpenes, led by 2.46% limonene and 1.69% caryophyllene, followed by linalool, humulene, and myrcene. Flower will normally contain much lower percentages than concentrates, and every harvest can differ.

No clinical evidence demonstrates that Double Burger itself treats pain, insomnia, anxiety, depression, or another medical disorder. Patients should use the cannabinoid and terpene analysis for the particular product they purchase and consult an appropriate healthcare professional when prescription medications or significant health conditions are involved.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Calling Double Burger pungent almost undersells it. The aroma has the dense, unmistakable funk associated with repeated GMO breeding, beginning with garlic and earth before expanding into diesel fumes, black pepper, onion, pine, and acidic citrus. Some phenotypes develop an almost chemical-cleaner edge, while others become more savory, with mushroom, fermented vegetation, or grilled-food characteristics appearing underneath the gas.

The flavor is surprisingly layered for weed with such an aggressive nose. Lemon can be brighter on the inhale than expected, followed by pine and pepper across the middle of the palate. Earth, garlic, skunk, and petroleum arrive more heavily during the exhale. A tested commercial expression describes the flower as earthy and spicy, with black pepper, lemon, pine, and a sharp cleaner-like aromatic quality.

Myrcene-rich batches may emphasize musky earth and herbs, whereas limonene can sharpen the citrus element. Beta-caryophyllene reinforces the dry pepper and woody spice that lingers after the sweeter notes disappear. Consumers searching for candy, berries, or creamy dessert flavors will find relatively little of that here. Double Burger belongs firmly to the savory, chemical, gas-heavy side of modern cannabis.
Growing Information

Double Burger is a photoperiod cultivar with an indoor flowering period of approximately 60 days, putting most phenotypes around the eight-to-nine-week range. Its growth reflects the mixed structure found throughout the GMO and Burger family: plants can stretch after flowering begins, yet mature branches are capable of supporting substantial, dense flowers. Growers should leave enough vertical space for the transition into bloom rather than treating it like a squat traditional indica.

Early topping or low-stress training can help spread the canopy and create more evenly illuminated flowering sites. A trellis becomes particularly useful as branches begin filling with weighty buds. Selective pruning below the productive canopy can also redirect energy toward the better-lit tops while improving air circulation through the center of the plant.

The dense flowers make environmental management important late in bloom. Humidity should be controlled carefully, especially as trichome production increases and the colas become tighter. Continuous airflow around and beneath the canopy reduces stagnant pockets of moisture that can encourage mold. Growers interested in hash production may find the genetics particularly appealing, since Double Burger sits within a breeding family repeatedly used for resin-focused cultivars.

Outdoors, plants should receive abundant direct sunlight and enough time to complete roughly eight to nine weeks of flowering after the seasonal transition begins. In many Northern Hemisphere climates, that places harvest around late September or early October, although local weather and phenotype can shift the finish. Once cut, a slow, controlled drying process is especially worthwhile. Rapid drying can remove much of the volatile lemon, garlic, and fuel character that gives this marijuana its unmistakable personality.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Double Burger?

Double Burger is GMO × Donny Burger, bred by Skunk House Genetics. Donny Burger itself contains GMO genetics, making Double Burger a concentrated continuation of the GMO and Burger family rather than an unrelated hybrid using the name.
Is Double Burger indica or sativa?

Double Burger is generally considered an indica-dominant hybrid. Its effects may begin with some cerebral activity and mood elevation, but physical relaxation usually becomes more pronounced as the experience progresses.
How strong is Double Burger?

It is typically regarded as high-potency cannabis. THC content varies widely between growers and batches, while some flower has tested above 30% THCA. One current commercial example reports 35.015% THCA, making cautious dosing particularly important for inexperienced consumers.
What does Double Burger taste like?

Expect a pungent combination of garlic, diesel, earth, black pepper, lemon, pine, and savory funk. Some phenotypes also reveal onion, mushroom, herbal, or chemical-cleaner notes inherited from the GMO-heavy lineage.
How long does Double Burger take to flower?

Indoor plants generally require approximately 60 days of flowering, or around eight to nine weeks. Growers should judge the final harvest date by trichome development and flower maturity rather than cutting strictly according to the calendar.
Final Thoughts on Double Burger

Double Burger is a concentrated expression of one of the most recognizable terpene families in contemporary cannabis strains . Instead of crossing GMO into something sweet or fruit-driven, Skunk House Genetics paired it with Donny Burger and effectively reinforced the same savory Chem-derived characteristics. Garlic, diesel, pepper, pine, lemon, earth, and strange onion-like funk dominate the sensory experience, while dense flowers and substantial resin production give cultivators plenty to work with.

The effects are equally unapologetic. A short cerebral lift can appear at the beginning, but the experience increasingly favors calm, physical relaxation, and a slower pace as the dose develops. That combination has made Double Burger valuable not only as finished marijuana but as breeding material for later cultivars such as Triple Burger and Hash Burger. For experienced cannabis enthusiasts who believe weed should smell loud, strange, gassy, and unmistakably dank rather than sugary and delicate, Double Burger is one of the clearest expressions of the modern Burger lineage.
